verdict: Red 7/10 ACCEPT-WITH-CUTS, blue 8/10 SUSTAINED with corrections that deepen it - concordant, and a clean example of a court that killed the CUSHION rather than the classification. The triage was right that TME is not cohort beta: it de-rated in four sequential, name-specific steps - the FY25 print down 28.8% on subscription deceleration PLUS a metric withdrawal, the Q1 print to a 52-week low on AI-piracy and ByteDance Soda fears, and the Q2 print down 8.5% over three sessions on a headline beat. The metric that would adjudicate the narrative was DISCONTINUED by management in March 2026, which is the disclosure fact that should have carried the most weight from the start: the withdrawal lands on the exact metric the priced narrative predicts damage in, and total paying users are now annual-only, next disclosed with FY26 results around March 2027. The triage's decisive reconstruction is assumption-free and correct: Q2-25 revenue solves to RMB8.441B, so stripping Ximalaya (closed 2026-05-18, RMB407M contribution) gives group ORGANIC revenue of +1.0% against +5.8% reported - 83% of the reported growth was inorganic. On membership specifically the prior-year base is RMB4.431B, so organic membership growth runs anywhere from zero to +2.5% depending on how much of the RMB407M landed in membership, and neither the PR nor the trade press disclosed the split. The triage named that split as the single input deciding the name and, to its credit, said it was knowable today rather than in November. Red resolved it. Ximalaya's own pre-listing HK prospectus shows subscriptions at 51.7% of revenue (stable at 51.1%, 50.8%, 51.7% across 2021-23), which puts roughly RMB210M of the RMB407M into membership and pins organic membership growth at about +3.4%, in a +2.6% to +4.3% band across a 45-60% subscription-share range. The triage's plus-or-minus 5pp uncertainty collapses, the bull branch ('organic membership held around 8%') is dead, and the deceleration sequence 17% to 13.2% to 8% to 3.4% is confirmed monotonic. Blue sustained the mix figure and added a caveat that cuts the right way: RMB407M over a 44-day stub annualizes to about RMB3.4B against Ximalaya's 2023 revenue of RMB6.16B, so either revenue roughly halved or a purchase-accounting deferred-revenue haircut suppressed recognized subscriptions - and a haircut would land LESS than 51.7% in membership, pushing organic toward the TOP of the band. Monotonic deceleration stands either way. The court's real work was on the cushion, and both benches converged after correcting each other. The triage claimed roughly RMB5.8B of total debt giving $5.7B of net cash at 41% of market cap, and about 5x EV to non-IFRS earnings - 'terminal-decline pricing for a business with intact gross margin, growing profit and a +16% live/IP engine.' Red pulled the actual borrowings: RMB5.997B current plus RMB7.142B non-current is RMB13.139B, 2.3x the triage's figure - the TENX cap-structure lesson verbatim, no borrowings pull before a net-cash claim. Blue then caught that RED had under-audited the same balance sheet it was correcting, missing RMB3,390M of non-current notes payable: total debt is RMB16,529M, about $2.44B, so net cash is $4.08B or roughly 30% of cap, not 41% and not red's 33%. On earnings, red annualized Q2 non-IFRS profit of RMB2.69B at $1.50B; blue corrected the conversion to $396M per quarter, or $1.58B. The two errors offset - red's understated debt and understated profit push the multiple in opposite directions - so the 5.9-6.4x range survived by luck rather than by arithmetic. Blue flagged this for the adjudicator explicitly, and it is the right instinct: a conclusion that survives two compensating input errors has not been verified, it has been lucky. Corrected, the picture is roughly 6.0-6.5x EV to non-IFRS earnings (about 6.1x, 5.9x crediting the roughly $327M UMG stake, about 6.5x stripping the interest income earned on the very cash the EV excludes) with a 30% net-cash cushion. That is a fairly-priced FADE, not terminal-decline mispricing, and both benches struck the triage's 'may already discount terminal decline' hook and cut court-worthiness from 7/10 to about 5/10. Two further items keep this from being ownable. The buyback - 43.5M ADS for $400M at roughly $9.20 average - is ABOVE the $8.66 tape and represents about 2.9% of cap; Tencent's supervoting control means minorities cannot force the $4.08B out, and the cash is onshore RMB with the transfer-restriction note unread. And the tape is 9.1% off a 52-week low at a 67.6% drawdown - new-low band, where desk falling-knife doctrine says re-review, never auto-buy. Orphan and RP_FAIR overrides do not apply: TME is a covered large-cap ADR, so 'fairly priced' is admissible as a finding rather than being suspect as a coverage artifact. The honest summary is that this was a correctly-identified deterioration whose only claim to court-worthiness was a cushion that turned out to be a third smaller and a multiple a fifth higher than pitched.
reopen_gates: 1698.HK interim report, due by 2026-09-30 - THE gate, and it is roughly six weeks out with three separate answers in one document: (a) the line-level Ximalaya allocation the US 6-K omits, which pins organic membership exactly rather than to a +2.6-4.3% band; (b) the business-combination note showing whether a purchase-accounting deferred-revenue haircut suppressed recognized subscriptions (blue's finding - a large haircut means reported organic deceleration is OVERSTATED and is grounds to re-court); (c) the composition of the RMB16,529M borrowings including the RMB3,390M of notes payable red missed.

Organic membership growth at or above +5.6% on the interim's actual allocation - i.e. Ximalaya contributing under RMB100M to membership - which would mean re-acceleration rather than the fourth consecutive step down. This is red's own change-my-mind threshold.

Restored paying-user and ARPPU disclosure. The March 2026 withdrawal removed the metric that adjudicates the narrative and made it annual-only; restoring it would be both an information gain and a governance signal.
A borrowings note reclassifying the RMB13.1B (or the corrected RMB16.5B) - the 20-F read on borrowings composition and cash transfer restrictions is owed and unread on both benches.
Cash-return run-rate above 6% of market cap. The current $400M buyback is about 2.9% of cap and was executed at roughly $9.20 against an $8.66 tape - it is not a floor.

PRICE GATE, per doctrine: the surviving objection is valuation (fairly-priced fade at about 6.0-6.5x EV/E with a 30% cushion), and valuation objections gate PRICE only. A multiple that discounts continued deceleration - rather than one that requires stabilization - is the entry condition, not a stabilization forecast.
